name: Ephraim
bio:
Ephraim is the second son of Joseph and his Egyptian wife Asenath. Joseph named him saying, "God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction" — commemorating that God blessed him with prosperity even in the land of his suffering (Genesis 41:52). On his deathbed, Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, as his own, giving them equal standing with his other sons to inherit as tribes of Israel (Genesis 48:5).

When blessing his two grandsons, Jacob deliberately crossed his hands, laying his right hand on the younger Ephraim instead of the firstborn Manasseh, prophesying that Ephraim's descendants would become greater than his older brother's (Genesis 48:13-20). This prophecy was indeed fulfilled — the tribe of Ephraim became so dominant in the history of the northern kingdom of Israel that the name "Ephraim" was often used to refer to the whole northern kingdom.

## 📖 Core Story: Mourning His Slain Sons

Generations later, the genealogical record preserves a moment of personal grief: two of Ephraim's sons, Ezer and Elead, were killed by the men of Gath when they came down to raid cattle. Ephraim mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him. When he and his wife later had another son, he named him Beriah, meaning "in trouble," because tragedy had struck his household (1 Chronicles 7:20-23).
